newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes subdued amid price volatility.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes subdued amid price volatility.

text.p: U.S. foreign crudes were subdued Wednesday despite the open transatlantic arbitrage as buyers waited out the day's price volatility, trade sources said.
Bellwether West Texas Intermediate for February soared 84 cents on the NYMEX, as traders, nervous over Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health, struggled to cover shorts.
"Prices were moving very rapidly and buyers stood aside," said a Midwest trader.
"Everyone just sat back and chuckled at the market," a Gulf Coast trader said.
The spread between February WTI and North Sea Brent narrowed somewhat before again widening to $1.80-85 a barrel, encouraging sellers to keep up the pace of transatlantic traffic.
"Demand is steady, but buyers are laying low in the weeds, because they figure they can get a better price if they wait," a Houston broker said.
February Brent to the Gulf Coast is on offer around March WTI minus 30 cents, traders said.

In Latin America, Colombia's state-owned Ecopetrol tomorrow is expected to award a Cusiana cargo for February 12-16 after accepting bids today. The price of Cusiana to the U.S. Gulf has plunged in recent days in response to the flood of North Sea and West African crudes on offer and generally weak demand.
In the U.S. aftermarket, a series of partial paper March Brent changed hands at $23.34/23.35/23.36/23.40 a barrel, down sharply from the IPE settlement of $23.55, traders said.
Feb/March Brent traded four times at 36 cents and once at 37 cents, up 11-12 cents from the London close.
